summary: A 1920s tree-crow's-nest site that became a 1933 L-4, then got a 1955 CL-160 cab moved here by helicopter in 1974 and now rents nightly.

facts.design: CL-160 flat-topped cab on steel I-beam tower

access.note: Forest Service rental lookout, booked via Recreation.gov

visit.trail_note: Reached by trail/road to the site per Recreation.gov listing; no water on site

events.note: L-4 cab built at the site, replacing an earlier tree crow's-nest lookout from the 1920s
Present CL-160 metal flattop cab first erected on Barkalow (Barklow) Mountain
Cab moved by helicopter to current site and placed on a steel tower; staffing began
Fire-season staffing at this site ended in 1996
Listed on the National Historic Lookout Register, March 31, 2003

evidence.quote: First put into service in the 1920s as a tree crows nest until a L-4 cab was built in 1933.

evidence.supports: 1955 CL-160 cab erected on Barkalow Mtn, moved 1974, steel I-beam 10' tower, rental
evidence.quote: The present CL-160 metal flattop cab was first erected on Barkalow Mtn. in 1955 and moved to this site in 1974. Now atop an unusual steel I-beam 10' tower, it is in the rental system.

evidence.supports: Ground house on Barklow Mountain flown by helicopter to site, placed on 12 ft tower in 1974, staffed 1974-1996
evidence.quote: The flat-roofed cabin was originally a "ground house" located on Barklow Mountain in the Powers Ranger District. It was flown by helicopter to its present location and placed on a 12 ft. tower and catwalk in 1974. It was then staffed during fire seasons from 1974 to 1996.

evidence.supports: One-room cabin sleeps up to four, amenities and no water on site
evidence.quote: The lookout is a one-room cabin, able to accommodate up to four people. It is equipped with a double bed with a mattress, a table and two chairs, solar lights, cleaning supplies and a fire extinguisher.

evidence.supports: Views of Pacific Ocean, Kalmiopsis and Wild Rogue Wilderness, Illinois and Rogue River canyons
evidence.quote: Lake of the Woods Lookout provides a panoramic view with vistas of the Pacific Ocean, the Kalmiopsis and Wild Rogue Wilderness areas, and the Wild and Scenic Illinois and Rogue River canyons.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR states a 10-foot steel I-beam tower, while Recreation.gov states a 12-foot tower and catwalk; the story notes both figures rather than picking one.

sources.title: Lake Of The Woods Lookout, Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest

notes_for_editor: Mountain name spelled 'Barkalow' by NHLR and 'Barklow' by Recreation.gov; treated as the same place, not flagged as a conflict. Tower height (10 ft vs 12 ft) differs between the two sources and is called out in the story and resolved_conflicts. Did not independently verify the exact trailhead/drive-up access; Recreation.gov implies a hike in with no on-site water.
